after.claim: **Witness (2): the kernel and the two lifts.** Since $V_A\cap qL''=q(q^{-1}Z[q])v=\mathbb Z[q]v$, the integral globalization map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(V_A\cap L'')/(V_A\cap qL'')=q^{-1}\mathbb Z[q]v/\mathbb Z[q]v$ is $(a_{-1}q^{-1}+a_0+a_1q)v\mapsto a_{-1}[q^{-1}v]$, which is onto with kernel $\mathbb Zv\oplus\mathbb Zqv\ne0$. The elements $g_1=(q+q^{-1})v$ and $g_2=(q+q^{-1})v+v=(q+q^{-1}+1)v$ both lie in $E_{\mathbb Z}$, both are fixed by $\psi$ because $\psi(q+q^{-1})=q+q^{-1}$ and $\psi(v)=v$, and both have residue class $q^{-1}v+qL''$; they are distinct since $g_2-g_1=v\ne0$. Hence the same nonzero crystal residue has two distinct bar-fixed integral lifts, and bar invariance plus congruence does not give uniqueness without the balanced isomorphism.

mathematical_review: An A-basis change with determinant minus one preserves the integral two-dimensional lattice. For the trivial witness, q^{-1}f belongs to qA_infinity precisely when q^{-2}f is regular at infinity, equivalently degree at most two. The residue quotient is the actual scaled polynomial lattice modulo the unscaled polynomial lattice, with generator the class of q^{-1}v; the same computed kernel and two lifts persist.
